```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`nb()` only calls the model's `predict()` on the validation data. What else
the object carries matters when you save it (e.g. with `saveRDS()`) or share
it: a saved `glm` is not just its coefficients.

## Five models on the same data

```{r fit, message = FALSE}
library(voipred)
library(bayespred)
library(kknn)

set.seed(1)
i   <- sample(nrow(gusto))
dev <- gusto[i[1:5000], ]
val <- gusto[i[5001:10000], ]

f  <- day30 ~ age + Killip + sysbp + pulse + pmi + miloc + sex
ff <- factor(day30) ~ age + Killip + sysbp + pulse + pmi + miloc + sex

fit_glm  <- glm(f, family = binomial, data = dev)
fit_bpm  <- bpmfit(f, data = dev, prior = log_f(m = 2))
fit_rf   <- ranger::ranger(ff, data = dev, probability = TRUE, num.trees = 500, seed = 1)
fit_knn  <- train.kknn(ff, data = dev, kmax = 50)
fit_svm  <- e1071::svm(ff, data = dev, probability = TRUE)
```

## What each object stores

| Model | What the object stores |
|---|---|
| `glm` | Coefficients; the QR decomposition (for the covariance matrix); fitted values, residuals, linear predictors and weights for every development patient; the outcome `y`; the development data twice: `data` (the whole data frame passed to `glm()`) and `model` (the columns used); the call, formula, terms and factor levels. |
| bayespred `bpmfit` | The posterior (coefficients, covariance matrix, family, terms, factor levels); the prior; the formula and call; `model`, the development data columns used (not stored with `bpmfit(..., model = FALSE)`). |
| `ranger` random forest | The trees (split variables, split values, child nodes, outcome counts in each leaf); the settings (`num.trees`, `mtry`, `min.node.size`); variable names and factor levels; the out-of-bag predicted risk of every development patient; the call. No covariates and no outcomes. |
| `kknn` nearest neighbours | The whole development data frame (all rows and all columns), because a prediction is made by finding the most similar development patients; the chosen `k`, kernel and distance; the fitted values; the call and terms. |
| `e1071` support vector machine | The support vectors: the covariate values of a subset of development patients, scaled, with the centring and scaling constants needed to undo it; their row numbers; their coefficients; the kernel parameters; the Platt-scaling parameters that turn scores into probabilities; the fitted class and decision value of every development patient; the call, terms and factor levels. |

Checking this on the fitted objects:

```{r check}
c(glm      = is.data.frame(fit_glm$data),
  bpmfit   = is.data.frame(fit_bpm$model),
  ranger   = any(c("data", "x", "y") %in% names(fit_rf)),
  kknn     = is.data.frame(fit_knn$data))

dim(fit_knn$data)          # the full development data
nrow(fit_svm$SV)           # development patients kept as support vectors

# the scaled support vectors can be turned back into the patients' real ages
age_back <- fit_svm$SV[, "age"] * fit_svm$x.scale$`scaled:scale`["age"] +
            fit_svm$x.scale$`scaled:center`["age"]
all.equal(unname(age_back), dev$age[fit_svm$index])

sapply(list(glm = fit_glm, bpmfit = fit_bpm, ranger = fit_rf,
            kknn = fit_knn, svm = fit_svm),
       function(m) format(object.size(m), units = "MB"))
```

## Sharing a model without sharing the data

What can be removed depends on whether the data is only *carried along* by the
object or is *part of the model*.

**Regression models (glm, bayespred): keep only what `predict()` needs.**
Prediction needs the coefficients, the terms and the factor levels, nothing
from the patients. Two details: the terms keep a link to the place the model
was fitted (if that was inside a function, the data comes along when saved),
and the `family` stored by bayespred's `posterior()` carries development data
when saved. Both are replaced with clean versions.

```{r share-reg}
share_glm <- function(fit) {
  out <- fit[c("coefficients", "terms", "xlevels", "contrasts", "rank")]
  out$qr     <- list(pivot = fit$qr$pivot, rank = fit$qr$rank)
  out$family <- binomial(link = fit$family$link)
  attr(out$terms, ".Environment") <- globalenv()
  class(out) <- class(fit)
  out
}

share_bpm <- function(fit) {
  out <- posterior(fit)                       # coefficients + covariance matrix
  out$family <- binomial(link = out$family$link)
  attr(out$terms, ".Environment") <- globalenv()
  out
}

rds_kb <- function(x) { f <- tempfile(); saveRDS(x, f); round(file.size(f) / 1024) }

# Does the saved object contain these exact numbers anywhere?
contains <- function(obj, values) {
  bytes <- paste(as.character(serialize(obj, NULL, xdr = FALSE)), collapse = "")
  any(sapply(values, function(v)
    grepl(paste(as.character(writeBin(v, raw())), collapse = ""), bytes, fixed = TRUE)))
}
some_ages <- dev$age[c(5, 17, 123, 999)]     # ages of four development patients

glm_shared <- share_glm(fit_glm)
bpm_shared <- share_bpm(fit_bpm)

c(glm_full = rds_kb(fit_glm), glm_shared = rds_kb(glm_shared),
  bpm_full = rds_kb(fit_bpm), bpm_shared = rds_kb(bpm_shared))   # KB on disk

# patient ages inside the saved object?
c(glm_full = contains(fit_glm, some_ages), glm_shared = contains(glm_shared, some_ages),
  bpm_posterior = contains(posterior(fit_bpm), some_ages),
  bpm_shared = contains(bpm_shared, some_ages))

z <- seq(0, 0.30, by = 0.01)
all.equal(nb(glm_shared, val, "day30", z), nb(fit_glm, val, "day30", z))
all.equal(nb(bpm_shared, val, "day30", z), nb(fit_bpm, val, "day30", z))
```

The shared versions give exactly the same net benefit, and the checked patient
values are not in them. `posterior(fit)` on its own still has them, through its
`family`. Note that
`butcher::butcher()`, which is often suggested for shrinking models, does
**not** remove the data from a `glm`.

**Random forest: already data-free.** Only the out-of-bag risks of the
development patients can be dropped:

```{r share-rf}
rf_shared <- fit_rf
rf_shared$predictions <- NULL
all.equal(nb(rf_shared, val, "day30", z), nb(fit_rf, val, "day30", z))
contains(rf_shared, some_ages)
```

**Nearest neighbours and SVMs: not possible.** Here the development patients
*are* the model: kNN predicts from all of them and an SVM from its support
vectors, so removing them breaks prediction. The options are to keep the model
where the data is and run the validation there (e.g. under a data-sharing
agreement or in a trusted research environment), or to choose a model type
that does not store patients.
